response.answer: NEVER SUMMER VALHALLA (MENS) 2027 — COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCT RESEARCH Note on the 2027 model year: The "2027" model year follows Never Summer's naming convention where the model year corresponds to the next season. As of April 2026, the 2027 model is available for pre-order from Australian retailers. The manufacturer's own website currently shows the "Men's 2026 Valhalla Snowboard" (which is the 2025/26 season board). The 2027 designation appears on the merchant site (Melbourne Snowboard Centre / Cherri Pow) for the upcoming 2026/27 season. The specifications listed by the merchant are consistent with the current production Valhalla specs. Reviewers have tested earlier model-years (2024, 2025, 2026) that share identical core specifications. IDENTITY & MANUFACTURER 1. Brand: Never Summer [1] 2. Model name: Valhalla [1] 3. Model year (merchant listing): 2027 [MERCHANT] 4. Product type: Snowboard [1] 5. Board category: Hard Charging Freeride [2] 6. Gender: Men's [2] 7. Manufacturer: Never Summer Industries [3] 8. Manufacturer founded: 1991 [3] 9. Founders: Tim and Tracey Canaday [3] 10. Manufacturing location: Denver, Colorado, USA [4] 11. Manufacturing method: Handcrafted in own factory [5] 12. Manufacturer distinction: Last larger, independently owned snowboard factory making boards in the USA, still family owned [6] 13. Manufacturer employees: Approximately 60 people [7] 14. Manufacturer reputation: Known for quality, durability, and innovation since early years of snowboarding [8] 15. First patent on hybrid camber technology: Awarded September 2010 [9] 16. Innovator of P-Tex sidewalls: Now a common feature on many manufacturers' boards [10] 17. Quality control: All boards go through an extensive 20-point inspection [11] FIRST AVAILABILITY & HISTORY 18. Valhalla design origin: Grew out of the classic, limited freeride board, the 2016 Twenty Five, celebrating their 25th anniversary [12] 19. LTD Valhalla first release: January 2023 — the limited version hit the market to rave reviews [13] 20. First full production model year: 2023/2024 season (model year 2024) [14] 21. 2027 model pre-order availability (AU): Estimated May 2026 [15] 22. 2027 model pre-order availability (Melbourne Snowboard Centre): Estimated June 1, 2026 [MERCHANT] PRICING & AVAILABILITY 23. Price (AUD, merchant — Melbourne Snowboard Centre): $1,049.99 AUD (Pre-order) [MERCHANT] 24. Price (AUD, Cherri Cherri Pow Pow — Jindabyne, NSW): $1,049.99 AUD (Pre-order, all sizes) [15] 25. Price (USD, manufacturer MSRP — neversummer.com, 2026 model): $709.99 USD (regular), on sale at $567.99 USD [16] 26. Price (USD, evo.com — 2026 model): Listed at sale prices from $567.99 [17] 27. Price (USD, Tactics — 2026 model): In stock [18] 28. Price (USD, Sun & Ski Sports — 2026 model): $567.93 USD [19] 29. Price (USD, V-Twin at $699.99 for context): The V-Twin (twin variant of Valhalla) retails at $699.99 MSRP [20] 30. Price (CAD, Ripping Giraffe — prior year): Was C$799.99, sold for C$559.99 (sold out) [21] 31. Availability at neversummer.com (2026 model): 147 and 153 in stock; 156, 160, 164 sold out [16] 32. Order status (merchant/2027 model): Pre-order [MERCHANT] 33. Supplier: evo.com (major US online retailer, price match guarantee, free shipping) [17] 34. Supplier: Tactics (US, free shipping over $150) [18] 35. Supplier: Blauer Board Shop (US specialty shop) [22] 36. Supplier: Salty Peaks Snowboard Shop (US) [23] 37. Supplier: Ski Pro AZ (US) [24] 38. Supplier: Shoreline of Tahoe (US) [25] 39. Supplier: Melbourne Snowboard Centre (Australia) [MERCHANT] 40. Supplier: Cherri Cherri Pow Pow (Australia, Jindabyne NSW, since 1987) [15] 41. Supplier: Snowboards.eu (European shop, Nidecker distribution) [26] 42. Supplier: Absolute Snow (UK) [27] 43. UK Distributor: Maxtrack (for Never Summer UK) [28] KEY SPECIFICATIONS (Manufacturer-verified) 44. Available sizes (manufacturer): 147, 153, 156, 160, 164 cm [16] 45. Available sizes (merchant, 2027 model): 153cm, 156cm, 160cm [MERCHANT] 46. DISAGREEMENT — available sizes: The manufacturer lists 5 sizes (147, 153, 156, 160, 164) while the merchant lists only 3 (153, 156, 160). This likely reflects limited pre-order availability rather than a size run change. 47. Shape: Directional [16] 48. Profile: Triple Camber Hybrid [16] 49. Flex rating: 8.5/10 [16] 50. Damp rating: 5/10 [16] 51. Width category: Mid-wide [16] 52. Mounting pattern: 2x4 [16] 53. Stance setback: 25mm [16] 54. Taper: 7mm [16] 55. Sidewall type: Sintered UHMW Polyethylene [16] 56. Core: NS SuperLight Wood Core (Poplar, Paulownia, Birch) [16] 57. Laminates: Full Recluse Carbon Web Layup, STS Pre-tensioned Fiberglass, Bi-Lite Fiberglass [16] 58. Topsheet: Co-Extruded Polymer [16] 59. Base: Durasurf XT Sintered 5501 Base [16] 60. Tail shape: Bat tail [29] 61. Tail protection: Aluminum reinforced tail [13] 62. Nose protection: Full wrap metal edge on the nose [13] 63. Edge technology: R.I.P. Edge-Hold Technology (Rocker Integrated Performance) [30] 64. Early-Rise Float Mechanics: Design feature for enhanced powder floatation [30] 65. Elastomeric Underfoot Stabilizers: For vibration absorption and high-speed stability [16] 66. Damping system: RDS 2 (three narrow laminated damping layers) [31] SIZE-SPECIFIC SPECIFICATIONS (Manufacturer) 67. Waist width 147cm: 24.7cm (247mm) [16] 68. Waist width 153cm: 25.7cm (257mm) [16] 69. Waist width 156cm: 25.9cm (259mm) [16] 70. Waist width 160cm: 26.0cm (260mm) [16] 71. Waist width 164cm: 26.2cm (262mm) [16] 72. Effective edge 147cm: 111cm (1110mm) [16] 73. Effective edge 153cm: 116cm (1160mm) [16] 74. Effective edge 156cm: 118cm (1180mm) [16] 75. Effective edge 160cm: 122cm (1220mm) [16] 76. Effective edge 164cm: 124cm (1240mm) [16] 77. Sidecut 147cm: Vario 665* (multiple radius average) [16] 78. Sidecut 153cm: Vario 714* [16] 79. Sidecut 156cm: Vario 722* [16] 80. Sidecut 160cm: Vario 756* [16] 81. Sidecut 164cm: Vario 783* [16] 82. Nose/tail width 147cm: 29.3/28.6cm [16] 83. Nose/tail width 153cm: 30.3/29.6cm [16] 84. Nose/tail width 156cm: 30.5/29.8cm [16] 85. Nose/tail width 160cm: 30.8/30.1cm [16] 86. Nose/tail width 164cm: 31.0/30.3cm [16] 87. Recommended weight 153cm: 54-72kg [MERCHANT] 88. Recommended weight 156cm: 63-90kg [MERCHANT] 89. Recommended weight 160cm: 72-100kg [MERCHANT] MANUFACTURER PERFORMANCE RATINGS 90. Freeride rating (manufacturer): 10/10 [16] 91. Powder rating (manufacturer): 9/10 [16] 92. All-mountain rating (manufacturer): 6/10 [16] 93. Freestyle rating (manufacturer): 2/10 [16] 94. Ability level: Intermediate/Advanced [16] 95. Rider level (evo classification): Advanced-Expert [32] 96. Flex category (evo classification): Stiff [32] TECHNOLOGY DETAILS 97. R.I.P. Edge-Hold Technology description: Integrates waves directly into the base plane of the board, not along the side edge, creating multiple high-pressure points for a smooth, drag-free ride [30] 98. Triple Camber Hybrid profile description: Three cambered zones — central camber between bindings and two additional camber sections near tip and tail, separated by subtle rocker areas [32] 99. Vario Power Grip Sidecut: Uses multiple radii (5 different radii) creating extra contact points to enhance edge hold [33] 100. Full Recluse Carbon Web: Full-length carbon web laminate (tip to tail) rather than just tip and tail, holding flex pattern integrity and creating powerful snap [34] 101. Carbon fiber angle: Bound at 20-degree angles for torsional stability and longitudinal rebound [35] 102. STS Pre-tensioned Fiberglass: Pre-hardened, pre-tensioned laminate with elastomer stringers between 0° and 90° glass fibers along effective edge [36] 103. Bi-Lite Fiberglass: Ultralight glass fiber matrix combining strength characteristics with lighter weight [37] 104. Durasurf XT Sintered 5501 Base: Developed by Crown Plastics exclusively for higher-end boards, with graphite added for speed [38] 105. UHMW P-Tex Sidewalls: More resistant to cracking in cold than ABS; Never Summer claims they've never seen one crack [39] 106. Co-Extruded Polymer Topsheet: Lightweight, scratch/chip resistant, fiber-backed thermoplastic with built-in stomp pad grip [40] 107. NS SuperLight Wood Core: CNC sanded to a fraction of a millimeter for tailored flex [41] 108. RDS 2 Damping: Lightweight three-narrow-layer system balancing freeride stability and freestyle liveliness [42] WARRANTY 109. Warranty period: 3 years from original date of purchase [43] 110. Warranty coverage: Free of defects in material and/or workmanship [43] 111. Warranty distinction: First 3-year warranty in snowboarding [44] 112. Warranty exclusions: Impact damage, abuse, misuse, normal wear and tear, stress/over-flexing [43] 113. Warranty applies to: Original purchaser from authorized dealer only [43] REVIEW RATINGS & RANKINGS 114. Manufacturer review rating (neversummer.com): 28 reviews, 100% 5-star [16] 115. Freeride ranking (SnowboardingProfiles.com 2025-2026): #2 out of 27 tested freeride snowboards [45] 116. Competitor ahead of Valhalla: Jones Flagship ranked #1 freeride snowboard [45] REVIEWER ASSESSMENTS — POSITIVES 117. Edge hold praise (consistent across all sources): Best-in-class edge hold on hardpack and ice [46] 118. Carving performance: Described as "a carving machine" by forum users [47] 119. High-speed stability: Very stiff and stable at speed [46] 120. Powder float: Above-average float in powder with surfy feel [46] 121. Versatility at varied speeds: Provides unexpected versatility when not ridden aggressively [48] 122. Crud/chop handling: Charges through chop and variable conditions [46] 123. Tree riding agility: Can turn incredibly fast in the trees; easy to maneuver in technical trails [49] 124. Confidence-inspiring: Compared to "drinking a cup of confidence" [50] 125. Base speed: Very easy gliding base; when well waxed can keep up with the best [51] 126. Lighter than expected feel: Felt lighter than normal for its class [51] 127. Flex pattern: Pretty consistent medium-stiff flex, a little softer in the nose [51] 128. Build quality/durability: Co-extruded polymer topsheet is very durable; base is super fast and ultra strong [52] 129. Aesthetics: Beautiful contrast with sleek, black topsheet and Viking graphic [53] REVIEWER ASSESSMENTS — NEGATIVES/CAVEATS 130. Learning curve: Takes a few runs to figure out; feels weird underfoot at first due to triple camber [53] 131. Not for beginners: Definitely not for beginners; requires aggressive riding [46] 132. Park performance: Spins, presses, and rails are a chore or nightmare; not a park board [54] 133. Pop limitation: Pop doesn't spring as much as Ripsaw, Shockwave, or Recurve Triple Camber profiles [51] 134. Flat-basing quirk: When one-footing and flat-basing, triple camber bends can sometimes interact inharmoniously [51] 135. Chatter on corn snow: Some chatter underfoot on corn/gravel snow conditions [55] 136. Weight in hand: Felt a bit on the heavier side in hand, though nimble on snow [56] 137. Cat-track drag: On cat tracks, if slightly on edge rather than flat-based, extra grip slows you down [57] 138. Size gap frustration: Reviewer noted 6cm gaps between sizes can leave riders between ideal sizes [58] 139. Not extremely damp: Very stiff and stable at speed but not extremely damp (moderate 5/10 damping) [46] 140. Binding sensitivity: Binding choice and stance setup make a huge difference; stiff bindings recommended [54] 141. Effort to initiate turns: Requires some effort to get edge to edge [53] 142. Switch riding: Decent switch for the setback, but not optimized for it [59] 143. Straight-lining limitation: Not a great straight-liner, but turny and grippy [51] COMPARISON TO NS LINEUP 144. Proto FR comparison: Proto FR sits between Valhalla and Swift; softer flex, easier to manage at slower speeds, more extensive damping [60] 145. Swift comparison: Swift has more rocker, 20mm taper (vs 7mm), and maximum powder float; more forgiving/surfy feel [60] 146. Cougar comparison: Cougar with Recurve Triple Camber carves harder but Valhalla is more stable [51] 147. V-Twin (twin variant): Takes the Valhalla and mirrors the tail shape to nose for a twin version [61] COMPETITOR COMPARISONS 148. Jones Flagship: Ranked #1 freeride board ahead of Valhalla at SnowboardingProfiles.com; flex 8/10, directional rocker profile [45] 149. YES PYL: Ranked #3 freeride board; exceptional value-for-money [45] 150. Capita Mega Death: Ranked #6 freeride board; big bomber for hard charging [45] 151. Jones Howler: New for 2025/26; freeride design with medium flex, surfy platform [62] 152. Burton Family Tree Sketch Artist: New 2025/2026 freeride entry [45] 153. Lib Tech Jamie Lynn: Ranked #9 freeride [45] 154. Capita BSOD: Ranked #10 freeride; more forgiving than Mega Death [45] 155. Similar boards per TheGoodRide: Amplid Souly Grail, K2 Alchemist, Burton Skeleton Key, YES PYL Uninc, Weston Backwoods, Cardiff Powgoda, Jones Mind Expander [59] DESIGN & CONSTRUCTION DETAILS 156. Camber profile for Valhalla: Modified triple camber with longer transition area in nose for better powder floatation and more forgiving surfy feel [63] 157. Base design: Printed P-tex base (unique for Never Summer); base designs and colors may vary [53] 158. Graphic theme: Viking/Norse mythology inspired design [53] USER EXPERIENCE INSIGHTS 159. Recommended stance width (reviewer, 156cm): Reference stance 535mm (21") [58] 160. Insert width at reference stance (156cm): 267/266mm front/back [58] 161. Typical test rider profile: 170lbs, 5'10", size 9.5 boot on 156cm fit well [46] 162. Larger rider report: 6'0", 185lbs on 160cm felt good [46] 163. Big rider report: 6'4", 230lbs, icy Midwest conditions — board grips and rips [46] 164. Expert endorsement: John Gerndt (creator of Burton Fish, 30+ years testing for Burton) reportedly called it "hands down the best board at the show" [64] SUSTAINABILITY & SOURCING 165. Material sourcing: Company prides itself on sourcing as many materials from U.S. as possible [44] 166. Sustainability commitment: Never Summer committed to environmentally responsible manufacturing practices [24] 167. Longevity/built to last: Boards built to last, reducing waste [24]
